questions.q: The impact force of a vehicle collision is proportional to the square of the speed.
Centrifugal force is the force that causes a vehicle to veer inward when navigating a curve.
questions.explanation: Centrifugal force causes the vehicle to veer outward, not inward.

questions.q: The creep phenomenon occurs in manual transmission vehicles as well.
questions.explanation: The creep phenomenon is specific to automatic vehicles.

questions.q: Automatic vehicles do not require clutch operation.
Compared to four-wheeled vehicles, two-wheeled vehicles appear farther away than their actual distance due to their smaller size.
Carrying a heavy load increases the reaction distance compared to normal conditions.
questions.explanation: A heavy load increases braking distance, not reaction distance.

questions.q: Worn tires increase stopping distance.
In a horn-use zone, the horn must be sounded when passing the crest of a blind uphill slope.
A short-term stop where the vehicle can be driven immediately without continuous stopping is considered stopping.
Loading or unloading cargo within 5 minutes is considered stopping.
Parking is prohibited within 10 meters of the intake of a fire-fighting water tank.
questions.explanation: Parking is prohibited within 5 meters, not 10 meters.

questions.q: Parking or stopping is prohibited on the left side of a safety zone and within 10 meters before and after it.
At a blind intersection with traffic control, I proceeded straight without slowing down.
After a traffic accident, even if there are no visible injuries or pain, a medical examination is necessary.
U-turns, crossing, and reversing are prohibited on highways.
The legal speed limit for three-wheeled ordinary vehicles on expressways is 80 km/h.
The legal speed limit for large special vehicles on expressways is 100 km/h.
questions.explanation: The legal speed limit is 80 km/h.

questions.q: The legal speed limit for towing vehicles on expressways is 100 km/h.
questions.explanation: The legal speed limit is 80 km/h.

questions.q: Vehicle-only roads are not highways.
When passing an obstacle, the vehicle on the side with the obstacle must yield to the oncoming vehicle.
Overtaking a vehicle that is overtaking a bicycle constitutes double overtaking.
questions.explanation: Double overtaking applies when overtaking a vehicle that is overtaking another automobile.

questions.q: Parking is prohibited within 3 meters of the entrance or exit of a parking lot or similar facility.
Parking or stopping is prohibited within 10 meters before and after a railway crossing.
Overtaking is prohibited within 50 meters before a pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Overtaking is prohibited within 30 meters before a pedestrian crossing.

questions.q: At night, the headlights of your vehicle and oncoming vehicles may make the situation near the road center less visible, a phenomenon called evaporation.
When driving in the rain, it is better to maintain a longer following distance than on clear days.
In a horn-use zone, the horn must be sounded when passing a blind intersection.
When an oncoming vehicle is far compared to when it is near, the blind spot caused by the oncoming vehicle is larger.
questions.explanation: The blind spot is larger when the oncoming vehicle is closer.

questions.q: For the purpose of repositioning, a taxi can be driven with a standard license.
Overtaking is prohibited on steep downhill slopes, but not on steep uphill slopes.
Except when unavoidable to avoid danger, sudden braking is prohibited.
When the driver is fatigued, braking distance increases.
questions.explanation: Fatigue increases reaction distance, not braking distance.

questions.q: If the railway crossing signal is green, stopping or safety checks are unnecessary.
questions.explanation: Safety checks are still required even with a green signal.

questions.q: Light vehicles cannot make a right turn on a blue traffic signal.
A yellow arrow signal allows only trams to proceed in the arrow’s direction, not other vehicles.
At a red flashing signal, vehicles and trams must stop temporarily and proceed after a safety check.
When a police officer’s hand signal differs from the traffic signal, the hand signal takes precedence.
Even if the road is wet, reaction distance does not increase.
When a vehicle stopped at a red signal does not move after it turns green, I sounded the horn.
questions.explanation: Sounding the horn in this case is considered misuse.

questions.q: After taking medication with sedative effects, driving must be avoided.
On a one-way road, if an emergency vehicle approaches and moving to the left would obstruct it, move to the right to yield.
The legal speed limit for ordinary motorcycles or motorized bicycles of 125cc or less when towing another vehicle is 30 km/h.
questions.explanation: The legal speed limit is 25 km/h.

questions.q: When passing a stopped kindergarten bus, proceed slowly and check for safety.
When there is a stopped vehicle in front of a pedestrian crossing, slow down and check for safety before moving ahead.
questions.explanation: You must stop temporarily and check for safety before moving ahead.

questions.q: When approaching a pedestrian crossing and it is clear no one is crossing, you may proceed without stopping.
Even if it is not raining, driving with a faulty wiper is prohibited.
On slippery roads, it is better to brake intermittently rather than applying the brakes fully at once.
When parking or stopping on a road with a roadside strip 0.75 meters or less in width, enter the strip and align with the left edge.
questions.explanation: Do not enter the strip; align with the left edge of the roadway.

questions.q: I rode a bicycle on a pedestrian-only roadside strip.
questions.explanation: Only pedestrians can use pedestrian-only roadside strips.

questions.q: I rode a bicycle on a roadside strip where parking or stopping is prohibited.
